title: Keyturn Roadside Assistance: Grant of the Term's Callout Allowance
content:
## How the allowance is put on the subscription

The term's callouts on a Keyturn Roadside Assistance subscription are granted in full when cover
begins and again at each renewal, and they are granted to the subscription rather than to the member. A grant adds the plan's callouts included in one
term.

A goodwill callout may be granted where the marketplace failed to attend within the plan's response
target, and it is granted as its own record so that goodwill and entitlement stay separable.

No callouts are granted while the subscription is suspended, and a subscription reinstated mid-term
resumes with the callouts it had rather than a fresh allowance.

### The three grants and the one refusal

| Occasion | What is added |
| --- | --- |
| Cover begins | The plan's callouts included in one term, in full |
| The term renews | The plan's callouts included in one term, in full |
| The marketplace failed to attend within the plan's response target | A goodwill callout may be granted, standing as its own record |
| The subscription is suspended | Nothing is granted while the suspension stands |
| The subscription is reinstated mid-term | Nothing fresh is granted; the subscription resumes with the callouts it had |

### Points of judgement

1. The allowance belongs to the subscription and not to the member.
2. A grant made when cover begins is the whole of the term's allowance, not a part of it.
3. Goodwill is expressed as "may", so a goodwill callout is open to the marketplace where it failed to
   attend within the plan's response target; and because it is granted as its own record, what was
   given as goodwill remains separable from what was granted as entitlement.
4. Reinstatement mid-term restores what the subscription had. It is not an occasion for a fresh
   allowance.
